On a page whose product is quotation fidelity, a garbled quote in a source label is a free hit for a defender.
holes.recommendation: Replace the label's quoted text with: "under Leo X, in the Lateran Council the question of revising the ecclesiastical calendar was discussed, it then remained unsettled, simply because the length of the years and months, and the motions of the sun and moon were held to have been not yet sufficiently determined" (Harvard Classics, Famous Prefaces translation).

holes.quoted_phrase: the ring-laser gyroscopes that now read the Earth’s rotation to better than a part in 10<sup>9</sup>
holes.description: Section 7's closing list gives three discriminating measurements; the first two carry dates that check out (Bradley's aberration published 1729, Bessel's parallax 1838) and the third carries a quantitative precision claim with no citation anywhere in `sources`. The figure is defensible — Di Virgilio et al., "Overcoming 1 part in 10^9 of Earth angular rotation rate measurement with the G Wettzell data", Eur. Phys. J. C (2022), arXiv:2208.09134 — but an uncited number in the sentence naming our strongest modern evidence is where an adversarial reader goes first, and this project has already been bitten once by a quantitative attribution that turned out to be unsupported (the A05 "Saturn's orbit" correction).
holes.recommendation: Add to `sources`: dict(label="A. Di Virgilio et al., “Overcoming 1 part in 10^9 of Earth angular rotation rate measurement with the G Wettzell data”, Eur. Phys. J. C 82 (2022), arXiv:2208.09134 — the ring-laser figure quoted in §7", url="https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.09134"). Leave the sentence as written; the number is right.

citation_failures: FAILED (contradicted): Hall, The Secret Teachings of All Ages, "The Sun, A Universal Deity". Our text says Christian festivals, the church calendar, eastward orientation and solar processions are not located in that chapter; sacred-texts sta11 contains the 25 December "birthday of the Solar Man" passage (with processions) and the Assumption-as-astronomical-festival passage. Our module docstring also cites the wrong file, sta12, which is "The Zodiac and Its Signs". Hall is not listed in `sources` at all.

FAILED (transcription): Copernicus dedication to Paul III, OSU PDF. Label quotes "when the Lateran Council the question of revising the ecclesiastical calendar was discussed"; the PDF reads "under Leo X, in the Lateran Council the question of revising the ecclesiastical calendar was discussed".

MISSING: the ring-laser precision figure in refutation §7 ("better than a part in 10^9") has no entry in `sources`. It is correct — Di Virgilio et al., Eur. Phys. J. C 82 (2022), arXiv:2208.09134 — but uncited.

UNCHECKED (not absent): the Internet Archive inside-the-book counts for item GallileoWasWrong ("liturgical" 0 hits, "calendar" 7 hits at scan pp. 49-51 plus a bibliography line) could not be re-verified on this pass. api.archivelab.org returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED and the djvu.txt stream returned only item metadata. The claim stays as the writer scoped it. Note separately that the archive item's own metadata identifies no volume or edition (uploader SUVRATSUT, 2017, description "ASTRO"); the Vol. I identification is the project's, consistent with A03, and I am not re-raising it.
VERIFIED: Tertullian, Apology 16 — both quoted phrases exact in the New Advent/ANF text.

VERIFIED: Catholic Encyclopedia (1911), "Orientation of Churches" — Gregory of Nyssa "the Orient contained man's original home, the earthly paradise" and Aquinas "Our Lord lived His earthly life in the East, and that from the East He shall come" both exact; the article confirms the major Roman basilicas "reversed this rule by placing the apse in the western extremity".

VERIFIED: Wikipedia, "Orientation of churches" — the Rome entrance-east sentence exact; "practically no relationship with the feast days", the 32-church Lower Austria/northern Germany study "with no general trend", the 43% figure, and "oriented approximately but not exactly to the geographical east" all exact.
VERIFIED: Wikipedia, "Liturgical east and west" — "churches are always described as though the end with the main altar is at the east, whatever the reality" exact.

VERIFIED: Wikipedia, "Computus" — one day of error per 310 years, four days out by the 16th century, ecclesiastical full moon drifting "more than three days every millennium", Bede noting the drift in 725, 21 March fixed. All exact.

VERIFIED: Wikipedia, "Gregorian calendar" — mean year 365.2425 d, Alfonsine value "365.2425463 days", Lilius and Clavius, 4 October 1582 followed by 15 October 1582. Our "a day in something like 3,300 years" matches the NASA figure the article gives (3,333.3); the article's own headline figure against the mean tropical year is 3,030 years, so "something like" is doing real work but is not wrong.

VERIFIED: British Library blog — the Bede quotation is verbatim and correctly cited to The Reckoning of Time, trans. Faith Wallis, 1999, p. 91, in the context of unequal day lengths, exactly as §6 describes.
VERIFIED: McCluskey, "Gregory of Tours, Monastic Timekeeping, and Early Christian Attitudes to Astronomy", Isis 81(1), 1990 — title, author, journal, volume, issue and year all correct.
VERIFIED: archive.org/details/haasedecursu — Gregory of Tours, De cursu stellarum, ratio qualiter ad officium implendum debeat observari, ed. Friedrich Haase, 1853. Latin title matches our label.

VERIFIED: Thony Christie, 28 October 2014 — Lilio "very definitely used the length of the tropical year, as determined by the Alfonsine Tables", and neither Copernicus's value nor Reinhold's Prutenic Tables. The trap the docstring records as avoided is correctly identified.

VERIFIED: scripturecatholic.com "Geocentrism" (dated 2017-08-13) and trueorthodoxy.org "Geocentrism" (Dormition Skete, 2022, ~40-50 sources) — both argue from scripture, the Fathers and the magisterium/experiments; neither runs a liturgical, calendrical, orientational or horological argument. As described.
VERIFIED: withthesun33.com/about-1 — 461 numbered items, the six item texts verbatim as we quote them, and no citation, footnote or source on any item.
reviews.summary: The verdict (NOT DEMONSTRATED), the no_source compression state and the KERNEL-tier steelman all hold, and I confirmed the no_source finding independently against a source the treatment never names: Sungenis's own "Sixty Ways to Refute a Catholic Heliocentrist" (March 2025) runs none of these six arguments. Fourteen of the sixteen citations check out verbatim, including every Bede, Tertullian, Catholic Encyclopedia, computus and Gregorian figure. One major defect: the published sentence saying Christian festivals, the church calendar, eastward orientation and processions are "not located" in Hall's solar chapter is false — sacred-texts sta11 carries both the 25 December "birthday of the Solar Man" passage and the Assumption-as-solar-festival passage, and our docstring cites sta12, which is a different chapter entirely. It does not move the verdict (Hall reaches a claim about the origin of a feast, never one about the Earth's motion), but it is the sweep's absence-claim failure in mirror image, in the rendered "No original to quote" block, in the same paragraph that invites readers to check us. Four smaller repairs follow: Tertullian is credited with denying the wrong proposition (he denies sun-worship, not that the practice is keyed to sunrise, and his next sentence is a tu quoque); "its own designers knew" is not supported by Bede, its only cited witness; the published search log covers only the geocentric half of the movement and never mentions Dubay or Skiba; and a garbled Copernicus quotation plus an uncited ring-laser figure. All six recommendations are supplied as drop-in replacement text.
